gen-gf-baumans-gf-cactus-classical-serif: Wrench-wide curves, drawn with unwavering lines: that is Baumans up top. And Cactus Classical Serif, a classic serif with gentle weight shifts, brings the dignity that keeps the pair authoritative.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-caudex: Baumans has a crescent-wrench c and diagonals as stout as its uprights, a rare, blunt look. But Caudex, a serif with gaping e mouths and only mild contrast, gives it a dignified partner.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-chiron-sung-hk: Chiron Sung HK is a text serif whose light modulation shows mainly when you look closely. Chiron Sung HK holds its own against Baumans, where every vertical and horizontal carries identical weight, and the difference is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-cinzel: Cinzel reads loosely tracked and spacious, with a modest gap between stems and hairlines and open c shapes. Baumans, with its rope-like constant strokes, supplies the weight.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia is a serif that keeps its apertures open even at tiny sizes, with stems just heavier than hairlines. Diphylleia lets Baumans, with its uniform strokes and wrench-wide c, be the loud one.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-donegal-one: Stout and showy, Baumans draws every curve without pressure swell at the corners. Donegal One, a classic serif with daylight in its curves, does the quieter work of reading well across words.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-fjord-one: Refined is how Fjord One feels, with wide-mouthed round letters and a gentle weight change in its bowls. Baumans makes the statement with ribbon-cut, uniform strokes, and Fjord One handles the reading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gentium-book-plus: Gentium Book Plus reads as a text serif, its horizontals a notch lighter than the uprights and its openings wide. Baumans is best at bold, uniform letters that announce themselves, while Gentium Book Plus does the patient work of moderate thicks and thins.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-gfs-didot: Literary in tone, GFS Didot moves with a subtle thick and thin cadence. Baumans does best with neon-tube constant strokes that command attention, while GFS Didot does best with generous curves that read smoothly.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-hahmlet: Dignified and editorial, Hahmlet has a slight charcoal-like pressure shadow, a classic serif with a widely parted c and s. Hahmlet can be sized up a touch beside Baumans' wirelike strokes, so its subtle weight differences stay lively.
